title: Spain voted out its king. Five years later, it was at war with itself.

beats.text: Spain voted out its king. Five years later, it was at war with itself.
April 1931. Republicans swept the city elections, and King Alfonso the Thirteenth left Spain. A republic was born.
beats.say: April nineteen thirty-one. Republicans swept the city elections, and King Alfonso the Thirteenth left Spain. A republic was born.

beats.text: It moved fast: land reform, army reform, church and state split. In 1933, women voted for the first time.
beats.say: It moved fast: land reform, army reform, church and state split. In nineteen thirty-three, women voted for the first time.

beats.text: But Spain was split down the middle. In 1934, miners in Asturias rose in revolt.
beats.say: But Spain was split down the middle. In nineteen thirty-four, miners in Asturias rose in revolt.

beats.text: The army crushed them, with a general named Francisco Franco directing from Madrid.
In 1936 the left-wing Popular Front won the election. Strikes, church burnings and political killings followed, on both sides.
beats.say: In nineteen thirty-six the left-wing Popular Front won the election. Strikes, church burnings and political killings followed, on both sides.

beats.text: In July, police officers murdered the right-wing leader José Calvo Sotelo.
Days later, generals rose against the Republic. The coup won in about half of Spain, and failed in the rest.
Franco's best troops were stuck in Morocco. Hitler and Mussolini sent planes, and flew them across.
By October, Franco led the rebels. The coup had failed. A civil war had begun.

beats.sub: Follow so you don't miss it
